## How to update the Pull Request Template

When updating the pr template, you must consider if updates need to be made to scripts/pr_compliance.py

## What are the files in workflows?
- bot.yml: Java CI. Spark lanes (JDK 11 on Spark 3.5, JDK 17 on Spark 4.2), Flink, bundle validation and integration tests. Runs on PRs, merge-queue groups and branch pushes; only push runs are path-filtered. Forks run it on every branch push; upstream it skips every job on pushes to branches other than master, release-* and branch-0.x, and every job but the aggregate on PRs from forks to master (see [Pull requests from forks](#pull-requests-from-forks)). Every test job depends only on the `Detect docs-only changes` job (`changes`), which runs on merge-queue runs only and makes the test jobs skip when the entry changes only files the push filter ignores (docs and images). The final `Java CI result` job aggregates the test jobs and reports on every PR and merge-queue run, so it can be required once the merge queue is enabled in .asf.yaml. The ASF GitHub Actions policy caps the jobs running at once in one workflow at 20 across all matrices, so `max-parallel` holds the two bundle-validation matrices back to keep the test jobs at 20 at once, and a change that takes them past 20 must lower it or serialize jobs; .github/ci/scripts/test-fork-ci-status.cjs checks the count. The transitional `Java CI Engines result` job mirrors `Java CI result` for the context branch protection required while Flink, bundle validation and integration tests ran in a separate workflow, and goes once branch protection no longer lists it. Dropped lanes are commented in place and marked `[CI-TRIM]`
- fork_ci_status.yml: Fork CI status. Mirrors the fork's bot.yml run for the head commit of each open fork PR to master onto the PR as the informational `CI (fork)` check. Runs when an upstream Java CI run completes and every 15 minutes for late runs and reruns. It never checks out PR code. Its tests, .github/ci/scripts/test-fork-ci-status.cjs, also cover the routing and concurrency of bot.yml
- fork_coverage_bridge.yml: Fork coverage bridge. Every 15 minutes, uploads to Codecov the JaCoCo reports that the fork's bot.yml runs stored as artifacts (through .github/actions/upload-coverage) for the head commit of each recently updated fork PR to master, and records each uploaded commit as a `Coverage (fork)` check. It never checks out or runs PR code; its tests are .github/ci/scripts/test-fork-coverage-bridge.cjs
- validate_source.yml: PR and Source Validation. One job, `validate-pr-and-source`, one of the two required status checks with `Java CI result`: it checks the PR description with scripts/pr_compliance.py, runs that script's own tests and the fork_ci_status.yml and fork_coverage_bridge.yml tests, validates the PR title, rejects commits with a Claude co-author trailer, and runs the source release checks (RAT, binary files, copyright). Never path-filtered, because a required check must report on every PR. Also runs on merge-queue groups, where only the source release checks apply

## Pull requests from forks

To reduce load on ASF's shared runners, pull requests from forks to `master` run the Java CI suites on your fork using your fork's GitHub runners, with lightweight checks upstream. To enable Actions in your fork:

1. Open the Actions tab in your fork and enable workflows before pushing.
2. Sync your fork and rebase your branch onto upstream `master` to include the current CI workflows.
3. Push your branch.

Each push runs the `Java CI` workflow on your fork, and the run appears in your fork's Actions tab. View results and rerun failed jobs there; the PR's `CI (fork)` check mirrors the run and may lag. A push that changes only docs or images creates no fork run, because the workflow path-filters push events. The PR's Codecov report arrives up to about 15 minutes after the fork run finishes, through the coverage bridge (fork_coverage_bridge.yml).

The `CI (fork)` check links to the fork run and is informational. When your PR is approved and added to the merge queue, Java CI runs using ASF's runners against the proposed merge with `master`, and skips its test jobs if the PR changes only docs and images. Release-branch PRs, and PRs from branches pushed to apache/hudi itself, keep upstream testing.
